Data preparation

The following code was run to prepare the dataset for analysis.

#removing duplicates
df <- df %>% distinct(track_name, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Filtering to only include Taylor's version songs from re-recorded albums
library(stringr)

albums <- c("Midnights", "evermore", "folklore", "Lover", "reputation", "Taylor Swift", "Taylor's Version")
pattern <- paste(albums, collapse = "|")

Taylor_version <- df %>%
  filter(str_detect(album_name, pattern) & !str_detect(album_name, "^Taylor's Version"))

#filtering out other 'playlists'
Taylor_version <- Taylor_version %>% filter(!grepl("Surprise Song", album_name))

Album analysis

As Taylor Swift has 12 albums (not including re-records, special editions, etcetera) and owns an incredibly large amount of songs, it might be interesting to see how the energy levels and loudness (dB) of her albums has varied throughout her career.

We might expect high energy songs to be louder as well… but lets see!

Energy

This boxplot shows that Taylor’s first album ‘Taylor Swift’ and her album1989 have the highest amount of energy. Folklore is by far the least energetic, but this might be due to the version of Folklore this dataset uses.

So what are her three most energetic songs?

track_name album_name energy
Haunted (Taylor’s Version) Speak Now (Taylor’s Version) 0.92
Tell Me Why (Taylor’s Version) Fearless (Taylor’s Version) 0.91
Better Than Revenge (Taylor’s Version) Speak Now (Taylor’s Version) 0.88
Out Of The Woods (Taylor’s Version) 1989 (Taylor’s Version) [Deluxe] 0.88

Loudness

The following boxplot shows how ‘loud’ Taylor’s albums generally are. Loudness in the dataset is measured in decibels (dB). In music the reference point for decibels is 0. At this 0 point the sound will be so loud that the music will be distorted. Therefore, the more negative the loudness, the ‘softer’ the music.

In the boxplot can be seen that Taylor’s loudest albums are ‘Taylor Swift’ and ‘Speak Now’. ‘Midnights’, ‘Folklore’ and ‘Evermore’ are on the quieter side.

What are her loudest songs?

track_name album_name loudness
Haunted (Taylor’s Version) Speak Now (Taylor’s Version) -1.91
Picture To Burn Taylor Swift -2.10
Sparks Fly (Taylor’s Version) Speak Now (Taylor’s Version) -2.35

Are energetic songs louder?

Based on this graph, it seems as though the higher the energy level in Taylor’s songs, the louder (dB) her songs are. It could be argued that Taylor purposefully chooses to increase loudness while recording energetic songs, to achieve these higher levels of energy.

Does she have albums that are generally louder and more energetic than her other albums?

It looks like Reputation, Red, Speak Now, Taylor Swift, 1989, Fearless and Lover are generally more loud and energetic. Folklore and Midnights on the other hand are calmer and quieter.

As we’ve seen Taylor’s loudest and most energetic song is “Haunted”.

What do you think of the song? Does this combination make it sound angry/aggressive?
